# Madrid Exam Study Plan: 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-05

A realistic plan for your Madrid schedule: **3 hours on weekdays**, **5 hours on weekends**, and lighter evenings on **Tuesdays/Thursdays** because of work. It balances problem-solving, writing practice, and spaced repetition so you can keep momentum without burnout.

## Weekly Study Schedule by Subject

| Week | Dates | Focus | Key Sessions | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | May 20–24 | Build foundations | Stats concepts + problem sets; Micro theory + diagrams; English outline practice; Programming syntax drills | Cover core syllabus once |
| Week 2 | May 25–31 | Reinforce and recall | Mixed review sessions; spaced repetition for stats/micro; English timed paragraphs; programming exercises | Improve recall and speed |
| Week 3 | Jun 1–5 | Exam-mode practice | Full mixed mock sessions; error review; short recall bursts; final light revision | Enter exams calm and prepared |

## Daily Study Rhythm

### Wednesday, Friday, Monday
- **Block 1 (90 min):** Main subject of the day
- **Break (15 min)**
- **Block 2 (75 min):** Second subject or practice set
- **Block 3 (15 min):** Spaced repetition review

### Tuesday and Thursday
- **Block 1 (75 min):** Deep work before work shift
- **Break (15 min)**
- **Block 2 (60 min):** Practice or writing
- **Block 3 (30 min):** Flashcards / formula recall / error log

### Saturday and Sunday
- **Block 1 (2 hours):** Hardest subject first
- **Break (20 min)**
- **Block 2 (2 hours):** Second subject
- **Block 3 (1 hour):** Review, flashcards, and planning next week

## Day-by-Day Plan

### Week 1: May 20–24
- **Wed 20:** Statistics foundations + 20-minute recap of microeconomics
- **Thu 21:** Programming basics + English writing structure; keep the last 30 minutes for review before work
- **Fri 22:** Microeconomics consumer theory + stats exercises
- **Sat 23:** Statistics problem set + programming practice
- **Sun 24:** English writing practice + microeconomics diagrams + weekly review

### Week 2: May 25–31
- **Mon 25:** Statistics mixed problems + spaced recall from Week 1
- **Tue 26:** Programming debugging + English timed writing
- **Wed 27:** Microeconomics market structures + stats formula recall
- **Thu 28:** English essay planning + programming exercises; short review session before work
- **Fri 29:** Statistics past questions + microeconomics review
- **Sat 30:** Full mock mix: stats + programming
- **Sun 31:** English writing + microeconomics + weekly error review

### Week 3: Jun 1–5
- **Mon 1:** Statistics final revision + weak-topic repair
- **Tue 2:** Programming final practice + English grammar and style review
- **Wed 3:** Microeconomics final recall + short stats quiz
- **Thu 4:** Light mixed review only; focus on flashcards and confidence
- **Fri 5:** Final exam-day warm-up: formulas, key definitions, and 1 short practice set per subject

## Spaced Repetition Plan for Memorization-Heavy Subjects

Use this repeat cycle for **statistics, microeconomics, and English writing**:

- **Day 1:** Learn the topic
- **Day 2:** 10–15 minute recall
- **Day 4:** Quick quiz or flashcards
- **Day 7:** Mixed review with old topics
- **Day 14:** Short test under timed conditions

Best use:
- **Statistics:** formulas, distributions, hypothesis testing steps
- **Microeconomics:** definitions, graphs, market structures, elasticity
- **English writing:** linking phrases, essay structure, common corrections

## Simple Progress Tracking Method

Use a very light system so it does not become another task.

### Daily tracker
For each study block, mark only one of these:
- **Done**
- **Partial**
- **Missed**

### Weekly check-in
At the end of Sunday, answer these 3 questions:
- What did I finish?
- What is still weak?
- What is the one priority for next week?

### Subject score
Give each subject a weekly score from **1 to 5**:
- **1–2:** needs urgent work
- **3:** okay, keep practicing
- **4–5:** exam-ready

### Rule to stay calm
If you fall behind, do not “catch up” by doubling everything. Instead:
- move unfinished work into the next available block
- keep the spaced repetition reviews
- protect sleep and breaks

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Copy weekly plan](https://calendar.google.com)
Action: [Button: Build study tracker](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets)

## Sources

- Spaced repetition overview: https://www.britannica.com/science/spaced-repetition
- Study planning and time management: https://www.mindtools.com/a4wo118/time-management
- Active recall and retrieval practice: https://www.learningscientists.org/blog/2016/6/23-1
